label: Deep refresh across all criteria (17 Nov 2026), including AI-generated works
description: Multi-language sweep across every catalog topic, 17 Nov 2026, plus a dedicated search for AI-generated films, shorts, vertical/micro dramas, YouTube/TikTok/Bilibili/Douyin series, AI anime, and AI comics/webtoons. Focus on titles new since the 16 Nov 2026 deep refresh, plus deeper and older titles not yet found, vertical dramas, and non-English works. Adults only; non-explicit notes; every entry sourced with a confidence label. AI-generated works are marked in format/meta and tagged AI-generated. This file was created at the start of the run and appended at the true end of SOURCES so existing IDs do not shift.

records.title: 9-Month Contract
records.meta: Feature documentary · Georgia / Bulgaria / Germany · Georgian · 79–80 min · directed by Ketevan Vashagashvili · original title ცხრათვიანი კონტრაქტი · world premiere at CPH:DOX 2025; US premiere at DOC NYC 2026
records.character: Zhana (a single mother in Tbilisi); her teenage daughter Elene appears as family, not as a sexualized character
records.summary: Official festival copy follows Zhana, a single mother working as a supermarket cashier, who becomes a surrogate for foreign couples to try to give her teenage daughter Elene a more secure life. Repeated pregnancies strain her health, and she tries to hide her changing body from Elene until her daughter begins to understand what is happening.
records.evidence: Official CPH:DOX and DOC NYC pages identify Zhana as an adult single mother in Tbilisi who is paid to carry pregnancies for foreign childless couples so she can support her teenage daughter Elene, and describe the film as a documentary portrait of that surrogacy work and their relationship.

records.title: Kashpirovskiy. Under The Spell
records.meta: Feature documentary · Poland / Czech Republic · 87 min · directed by Łukasz Konopa · original title Kaszpirowski · Czech premiere at Ji.hlava 2026
records.character: Soviet and post-Soviet television audiences; official festival copy also notes televised procedures on women without anaesthetic
records.summary: A documentary portrait of Anatoly Kashpirovsky, a hypnotist and TV healer who became a mass-audience figure at the end of the Soviet era. Official festival copy describes televised healing séances that reached hundreds of millions, including operations on women without anaesthetic, and follows his later attempt at an internet-era comeback.
records.method: Televised mass hypnosis and healing séances
records.evidence: Official Ji.hlava 2026 program page and a Variety report both describe Kashpirovsky as a mass-hypnosis / television-healer figure whose séances reached a Soviet audience of hundreds of millions, including televised procedures on women without anaesthetic.
